Hi Olivia — great call today, thanks for walking us through the FinTechCo objectives. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed POC scope, evaluation plan, and ownership so we’re aligned before we kick off. Attaching a working spreadsheet with measurable success criteria.

High-level POC scope (2 weeks):
- Use case A: Batch invoice classification + entity extraction (baseline dataset you provided)
- Use case B: Chat-assisted reconciliation queries (demo flows you showed)

Proposed success criteria (draft):
1) Classification accuracy: >= 92% F1 on holdout test set for Use case A
2) Extraction NER precision >= 90% and recall >= 88% on sample corpus
3) Chat latency: median response < 300ms for 95th percentile of typical queries
4) Stability: no more than 2 failures per 1k requests during test window

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (prep): data ingestion + mapping (owner: FinTechCo + Redwood SE)
- Week 1: model integration, baseline runs, metric collection (owner: Dylan)
- Week 2: tuning, acceptance test, handover (owner: Marissa/Ava)

Ownership & next steps:
- Tech lead: Dylan Brooks (redwood) — integration, test harness, metric capture
- Commercial/POC owner: Marissa Cole (redwood) — success criteria, timelines, executive check-ins
- FinTechCo data lead: Olivia Chen — provide labels/samples and access to sandbox environment

Proposed kickoff: Tue, Mar 2 at 10:00 AM PT — please confirm.

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria_v1.xlsx (working draft)

Thanks — I’ll update this doc with any edits from your side.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the clear criteria. Two quick items from our side after reviewing the spreadsheet:

1) Add use case C: real-time fraud signal enrichment. Our fraud team wants to see whether Redwood can enrich streaming events with model predictions and meet tail-latency targets. This is a high-priority add.
2) Can we add data retention and audit log visibility as part of the acceptance criteria? Security needs to confirm retention windows and access logs for the trial data.

If possible we’d also like an extra week for the trial to validate the streaming case (so 3 weeks total). Let me know what that means for timelines and any impacts to cost.

We’re happy to proceed once the plan is updated — procurement is on copy to help with contracting and any NDAs.

Marissa / Ava — quick tech assessment: adding Use case C (real-time fraud enrichment) is doable within the POC but requires the following tradeoffs / changes:

- Integration work: we’ll need a small streaming harness (consumer -> enrichment -> return) and a synthetic event stream for load tests (owner: Dylan).
- Acceptance metric for streaming: 95th percentile latency < 250ms, end-to-end (ingest -> model -> return) on the sandbox network.
- Data retention/audit logs: we can surface request/response logs and retention policy for the trial (retention window: 30 days by default, configurable).
- Infra impact: recommend a short-lived dedicated instance for streaming tests to ensure stable latency during the POC; this adds 1 week to the schedule and a modest cost bump (estimate in attached proposal).

Revised timeline (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): data + stream schema, access, synthetic event generation
- Week 1: baseline batch runs + chat flows
- Week 2: streaming integration & latency validation
- Week 3: tuning, acceptance tests, audit/log verification

I’ve attached an updated proposal outlining the infra changes and estimate: Redwood_POC_Proposal_v2.pdf. If you want, I can scope a smaller-capacity streaming run to reduce cost but that may affect the 95th percentile guarantee.

Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
